Formula: Euclidean Distance Formula
Exact Expression: d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2 + (z_2 - z_1)^2}
Definitions: Metric distance between two points in three-dimensional Euclidean space R^3.
Derivation/Reference: Derived from Pythagorean theorem applied successively in orthogonal coordinate planes; Rene Descartes, La Geometrie (1637)
Example: P1=(0,0,0), P2=(1,2,2) -> d = sqrt(1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(9) = 3
Domain: coordinate_geometry
Assumptions: Flat Euclidean geometry metric g_ij = delta_ij
Common Errors: Confusing difference order (x2 - x1) with addition
subject: Euclidean Distance Formula
